verdict.rationale: The evidence shows llama.cpp is a local C/C++ inference engine that users describe as self-hosted. It never documents a policy, control, or guarantee that user data is not collected or used for training, so on-device execution is only an implied architectural property, not an evidenced capability for this story. A privacy posture on training data is a fair question for an AI tool, so the axis applies and absence of evidence is "none".

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models
